lect: Seoul Korean and Northern Hamkyeong Korean
claim: Word-initial /L/ shows seven phonetic variant types in both Seoul Korean and Northern Hamkyeong Korean rather than a single invariant realization. Dialect shifts their proportions: Seoul speakers use lateral [l] and approximant [ɹ] more often, whereas Northern Hamkyeong speakers use trill [r] and obstruent realizations more often.

source_forms.reported_variants: seven types total; article abstract/highlights explicitly identify tap, nasal, lateral, approximant, obstruent and trill among the observed variants

scope: elicited word-initial /L/ in loanword and Sino-Korean reading materials
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source reports the same broad variant inventory in both dialect groups; dialect differences are proportional, not categorical presence/absence statements.

claim: Seoul Korean shows an age effect in word-initial liquid realization: younger speakers produce the lateral [l] more often than older speakers, consistent with an ongoing shift in the loanword-compatible initial-liquid allophony.

source_forms.direction: younger Seoul speakers -> more [l] word-initially than older Seoul speakers

normalized_environment: P(INITIAL_LATERAL) higher in YOUNGER SEOUL speakers
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Age changes probabilities rather than defining separate categorical grammars.

time_scope: North Korean speakers resident in Seoul, stratified by age/contact
claim: Northern Hamkyeong speakers show both age and contact conditioning of word-initial /L/: trill use declines among younger speakers, and speakers with longer residence/more contact in South Korea tend to produce fewer obstruent realizations.

source_forms.age_direction: younger Northern Hamkyeong speakers -> fewer trills
source_forms.contact_direction: longer/more South-Korean contact -> fewer obstruent realizations

formal_environment: /L/ -> [r] or obstruent / #__, conditioned by age and dialect contact
normalized_environment: INITIAL_LIQUID variant probabilities track AGE + CONTACT in NORTHERN_HAMKYEONG
scope: Northern Hamkyeong speakers living in Seoul
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source describes partial dialect acquisition, not complete convergence on Seoul Korean.

lect: Seoul Korean versus Northern Hamkyeong Korean
claim: The experiment deliberately contrasts lexical/domain status: liquid-initial loanwords are licit for both dialect groups, whereas liquid-initial Sino-Korean forms written in North Korean orthography are unfamiliar/phonotactically conflicting for Seoul speakers. The latter condition tests whether Seoul speakers productively apply native initial-liquid avoidance to novel written inputs.

stimulus_strata: loanwords with licit initial liquids in both dialect groups
Sino-Korean words shown in North Korean orthography with initial liquid

formal_environment: #L in LOAN versus SINO_KOREAN test items
normalized_environment: INITIAL_LIQUID licensing depends on LEXICAL_STRATUM and DIALECT; experimental novel-orthography condition probes productivity
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The experimental condition should not be mistaken for naturally established Seoul lexical items; it is a productivity probe.
